question: Estimate the number of distinct job postings published in the United States during calendar year 2026 (2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31) for new-graduate roles — summer internships plus full-time entry-level positions for new bachelor's or master's graduates with 0–1 years of experience, in professional (white-collar) occupations — whose posting text explicitly states that the employer will sponsor a work visa (for example "H-1B sponsorship available" or "visa sponsorship provided"). Count each posting once even if it appears on several job boards. Do not count postings that do not state sponsorship in their text, even if the employer has sponsored visas before or ticks a "will sponsor" box on a job platform, and do not count postings that rule sponsorship out.

target.what: Distinct unique job postings published in the United States during calendar year 2026 for new-graduate roles (summer internships plus full-time entry-level positions for new bachelor's or master's graduates with 0–1 years of experience) in professional white-collar occupations, whose posting text ex
target.publisher: No official publisher; constructed estimate from job-board, employer, and administrative evidence
target.caveats: The target period is partly future relative to the 2026-10-28 cutoff: January–October 2026 is observed/observable, November–December 2026 must be forecast or extrapolated. 'Distinct' requires deduplication across boards; most job-board counts are posting-events, not unique postings, so a deduplicati

candidates.perspective: Job-board aggregator (e.g., Indeed, LinkedIn, Glassdoor, Handshake, WayUp, Simplify, RippleMatch)
candidates.hypothesis: Total unique new-graduate professional postings in 2026 multiplied by the share whose text explicitly mentions visa sponsorship yields the target. The share is the key bridge; aggregator totals give the base.
candidates.data_to_find: Annual or monthly counts of unique new-graduate/entry-level professional postings in the US for 2025 and available 2026 months from major boards; any published share of postings mentioning 'visa sponsorship', 'H-1B', or 'sponsorship available'. Minimum evidence: one credible total and one sponsorship-mention share with scope and period.
search_hints: new grad job postings 2025 total United States
share of job postings mentioning visa sponsorship
LinkedIn entry level jobs United States count 2025

candidates.perspective: Sponsorship-focused job boards and trackers (e.g., MyVisaJobs, H1BGrader, Simplify, Built In, Levels.fyi job board)
candidates.hypothesis: Boards that filter specifically for sponsorship-mentioning postings provide a direct partial count of the target; scaling by their coverage of the overall new-grad market gives the total.
candidates.data_to_find: Counts of active or annual sponsorship-mentioning new-grad/entry-level postings on sponsorship-filtered boards for 2025 and 2026 months; their stated coverage or overlap with the broader market. Substitute: counts of 'H-1B sponsorship' tagged postings on general boards.
search_hints: H1B sponsorship jobs new grad count
MyVisaJobs new graduate postings 2025
visa sponsorship filter job board number of jobs

candidates.hypothesis: H-1B registrations, LCA filings, and OPT/STEM-OPT approvals bound the population of new-grad roles that actually sponsor; the ratio of sponsorship-mentioning postings to actual sponsored hires (postings per sponsored hire) converts administrative flows into posting counts.
candidates.data_to_find: H-1B cap registrations and selections for FY2026/FY2027, LCA filings by occupation and entry-level wage level, OPT and STEM-OPT approval counts for 2025–2026. Minimum evidence: one flow (e.g., entry-level LCAs) and a postings-per-hire ratio from a comparable employer or survey.
search_hints: H-1B registrations FY2027 number
LCA filings entry level wage level 1 2025
OPT approvals 2025 STEM OPT count

candidates.perspective: Large employers and campus recruiting teams
candidates.hypothesis: Sum over major sponsoring employers of (new-grad openings × share of postings stating sponsorship) plus a long tail allowance. Employer recruiting volumes and sponsorship policies are observable; the share of their postings that state sponsorship is the bridge.
candidates.data_to_find: New-grad/intern hiring volumes for top sponsoring employers (tech, consulting, finance, engineering) in 2025–2026; their stated sponsorship policies for entry-level roles; number of distinct postings per opening. Minimum evidence: hiring volumes for a set of large employers and a postings-per-opening ratio.

candidates.data_to_find: Text-mining or survey estimates of the percentage of US job postings (especially entry-level/professional) that mention visa sponsorship or H-1B; any breakdown by occupation, degree level, or experience. Minimum evidence: one sample-based share with methodology and period.

candidates.hypothesis: If any sponsorship-mentioning new-grad posting counts exist for 2023–2025, their level and growth rate project 2026, adjusted for hiring-cycle and policy shocks (e.g., H-1B fee changes, immigration policy).
candidates.data_to_find: Annual counts of sponsorship-mentioning new-grad postings for 2023, 2024, 2025 from any consistent source; monthly seasonality (internship postings peak in fall/winter, full-time in fall). Minimum evidence: two aligned annual observations from the same source.

candidates.hypothesis: 2025–2026 immigration policy changes (H-1B fees, lottery rules, travel bans) and tech hiring cycles shift both the number of sponsoring employers and the propensity to state sponsorship in postings; quantifying exposure adjusts the base rate.
candidates.data_to_find: Policy changes effective 2025–2026 affecting H-1B/OPT and employer sponsorship; evidence on employer responses (postings removing sponsorship language, hiring freezes). Minimum evidence: one measured change in sponsorship-mention share or sponsoring-employer count around a policy date.

Minimum evidence: applications-per-posting ratio and total application volume for new-grad roles.

a1.role: Adjustment factor for new-grad professional scope relative to all full-time postings

methods.rationale: Base total of new-grad professional postings times the Handshake 2026 sponsorship share, adjusted for the new-grad professional scope. The Handshake share is the best available direct measure of stated sponsorship in posting text; the adjustment factor accounts for the difference between all full-time postings and new-grad professional postings. Main failure mode: the base total a2 is not directly observed and the adjustment a1 is uncertain.

p159.role: Total approvals for H-1B petitions for initial employment, FY 2025

a3.role: Ratio of sponsorship-mentioning postings to initial H-1B approvals

This bounds the population of roles that actually sponsor and converts it to a posting count. Main failure mode: the ratio a3 is not directly observed and the FY2025 approvals are a lagged proxy for 2026 posting behavior.

assumptions.name: Share of new-grad professional postings stating sponsorship, relative to all-posting Handshake rate
assumptions.rationale: Handshake's 2.6% is for full-time postings on an early-career platform; new-grad professional postings are more concentrated in sponsoring sectors (tech, finance, consulting) than all postings, but the 2026 policy shock ($100k fee, 39-country travel ban) suppressed stated sponsorship. JobShifu's 0.18% all-posting rate suggests the true new-grad rate could be well below 2.6%. Range spans 0.4x to 2.5x of the Handshake rate.
assumptions.applies_when: The Handshake 2.6% figure is used as the base rate for new-grad professional postings.
assumptions.falsified_by: A new-grad-specific text-mining study showing the share is below 1% or above 6%.

assumptions.name: Total unique US new-grad professional postings in 2026 (internships + entry-level)
assumptions.rationale: No kept point gives this base directly. Handshake postings are down 15-16% YoY and down 12% vs 2019-20; NACE forecasts +4% interns and +5.6% new grads. A base of ~800k unique new-grad professional postings is consistent with a platform like Handshake covering a large share of the market. Range is wide because the base is not directly observed.
assumptions.applies_when: Used as the base for the share-based route.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published count of unique new-grad professional postings for 2025 or 2026 outside the 300k-2M range.

assumptions.name: Ratio of sponsorship-mentioning postings to initial H-1B approvals
assumptions.rationale: Each initial H-1B approval corresponds to at least one posting, but many postings are for roles that do not result in an approval (lottery loss, candidate decline, multiple postings per hire). A ratio of 3 postings per approval is a central guess; range 1-10 reflects uncertainty in posting-to-hire conversion.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert FY2025 initial H-1B approvals into a posting count.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that the posting-to-approval ratio is below 1 or above 20.

assessment.note: All restate the same Handshake/CNBC figure: 2.6% of full-time US postings offered visa sponsorship in 2026. One underlying measurement, many syndicated URLs; counts as a single independent source.
Same Handshake series: 10.9% in 2023. Establishes the 2023 baseline for the same measurement, not an independent estimate.

Trylitos internship subset: 0.4% of 984 internship postings offer sponsorship — the only new-grad-specific sponsorship-offer rate in the evidence, and it is higher than the all-posting rate in the same sample.

Three independent measurements of 'share of US postings stating sponsorship' differ by 26x (2.6% vs 0.18% vs 0.1%). Differences are scope (Handshake is early-career/full-time only; JobShifu and Trylitos are all postings including hourly/blue-collar) and text-mining strictness. Not a contradiction of fact but a large definitional spread that must be carried as uncertainty.

p279.role: Total US job postings read in JobShifu snapshot (all-posting stock, Oct 2026)

a6.role: Ratio of total unique US new-grad professional postings in 2026 to the JobShifu all-posting snapshot size

p313.role: Share of full-time US postings offering visa sponsorship, 2026 (Handshake)

a1.role: Ratio of new-grad professional sponsorship-mention rate to the all-full-time Handshake rate

methods.rationale: Base times share. The base is the JobShifu all-posting snapshot (p279, 1,482,236) scaled by a6 to the new-grad professional annual flow; the share is the Handshake 2.6% (p313) adjusted by a1 to the new-grad professional scope. Shared dependency: any error in the Handshake 2.6% propagates directly. Failure mode: if Handshake's 2.6% is measured on a different population (e.g. only postings that tick a sponsorship box rather than state it in text), the route is biased.

p159.role: Total approvals for H-1B petitions for initial employment, FY 2025 (approval count, converted to postings by a3)

a3.role: Sponsorship-mentioning postings per initial-employment H-1B approval

methods.rationale: Administrative-flow route: FY2025 initial-employment H-1B approvals (114,806) times postings per approval. This is independent of the Handshake/JobShifu share measurements. Failure modes: FY2025 approvals are a lagged proxy for 2026 sponsorship activity (the $100,000 fee and the 38.5% drop in FY2027 registrations suggest 2026 sponsorship is lower, so this route may be biased high); and the postings-per-approval ratio is poorly measured.

p279.role: Total US job postings read in JobShifu snapshot

p761.role: Share of postings stating visa sponsorship is available (JobShifu)

a4.role: Adjustment from all-posting JobShifu scope to new-grad professional scope

methods.rationale: JobShifu snapshot count times its offer share, scaled up to the new-grad professional scope. The snapshot is a point-in-time stock of ~1.48M postings, not an annual flow, so this route implicitly assumes the snapshot is representative of the annual posting flow in composition; that is a strong assumption and a key failure mode. The a4 multiplier is the bridge from all-posting to new-grad professional scope.

p39.role: Count of US postings labelled US by the API at read time, 29 September 2026 (all-posting pool)

a7.role: Ratio of total unique US new-grad professional postings in 2026 to the Trylitos US-labelled posting pool

a5.role: Share of 2026 new-grad professional postings that are internships rather than full-time entry-level

p924.role: Share of US internship postings offering sponsorship, September 2026 (Trylitos)

p313.role: Share of full-time US postings offering visa sponsorship, 2026 (Handshake)

a1.role: Ratio of new-grad professional sponsorship-mention rate to the all-full-time Handshake rate

methods.rationale: Sums the two channels that make up the target: internships (base times internship share times the Trylitos internship offer rate p924) and full-time entry-level (base times the complement times the Handshake rate adjusted by a1). The base is the Trylitos US-labelled posting pool (p39, 68,467) scaled by a7 to the new-grad professional annual flow. The internship rate p924 is the only new-grad-specific sponsorship-offer measurement in the evidence, but it comes from a small September 2026 sample (984 postings) and a different text-mining method than Handshake. Shared dependencies: a1 and p313 are shared with m1, so m1 and m4 are not independent routes.

assumptions.name: Ratio of new-grad professional sponsorship-mention rate to the all-full-time Handshake rate
assumptions.rationale: Handshake's 2.6% is measured on full-time postings on an early-career platform, close to but not identical to the target scope. The Trylitos internship subset shows a higher offer rate (0.4%) than the all-posting rate in the same sample (0.1%), and JobShifu's professional functions (software 0.81%, education 1.11%) are several-fold above the all-posting 0.18%, suggesting new-grad professional postings state sponsorship more often; but the target excludes non-professional postings Handshake may include. Net effect uncertain, centred at 1 with a wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to move the Handshake all-full-time rate onto the new-grad professional scope.
assumptions.falsified_by: A direct new-grad-specific sponsorship-mention rate materially outside 0.4x-2.5x of 2.6%.

assumptions.name: Sponsorship-mentioning postings per initial-employment H-1B approval
assumptions.rationale: Each initial H-1B approval corresponds to at least one posting that stated sponsorship, but postings are reposted, duplicated across boards, and many sponsorship-mentioning postings never convert to an approval (lottery losses, candidates who do not need sponsorship, roles filled by OPT workers). A ratio of a few postings per approval is the natural order of magnitude; the range spans the plausible deduplication and conversion spread.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert FY2025 initial H-1B approvals into a 2026 posting count, assuming the FY2025 approval level is a reasonable stand-in for 2026 sponsorship activity.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that sponsorship-mentioning postings per approval are below 1 or above 10.

assumptions.name: Adjustment from all-posting JobShifu scope to new-grad professional scope
assumptions.rationale: JobShifu measures sponsorship mentions across all US postings, including hourly and blue-collar roles that almost never sponsor. New-grad professional roles (software, data, engineering, finance, consulting) are far more likely to state sponsorship than the all-posting average, so the all-posting rate must be scaled up. previous_methods.rationale: Administrative-flow route: FY2025 initial-employment H-1B approvals (114,806) times postings per approval. This is independent of the Handshake/JobShifu share measurements. Failure modes: FY2025 approvals are a lagged proxy for 2026 sponsorship activity (the $100,000 fee and the 38.5% drop in FY2027 registrations suggest 2026 sponsorship is lower, so this route may be biased high); and the postings-per-approval ratio is poorly measured.

a4.role: Adjustment from all-posting JobShifu scope to new-grad professional scope

previous_methods.rationale: JobShifu snapshot count times its offer share, scaled up to the new-grad professional scope. The snapshot is a point-in-time stock of ~1.48M postings, not an annual flow, so this route implicitly assumes the snapshot is representative of the annual posting flow in composition; that is a strong assumption and a key failure mode. The a4 multiplier is the bridge from all-posting to new-grad professional scope.

p1.role: Share of full-time US postings offering visa sponsorship, 2026 (Handshake)

a1.role: Ratio of new-grad professional sponsorship-mention rate to the all-full-time Handshake rate

previous_methods.rationale: Sums the two channels that make up the target: internships (base times internship share times the Trylitos internship offer rate p32) and full-time entry-level (base times the complement times the Handshake rate adjusted by a1). The base is the Trylitos all-posting sample (p29) scaled by a7 to the new-grad professional annual flow. The internship rate p32 is the only new-grad-specific sponsorship-offer measurement in the evidence, but it comes from a small September 2026 sample (984 postings) and a different text-mining method than Handshake. Shared dependencies: a1 and p1 are shared with m1, so m1 and m4 are not independent routes.

previous_assumptions.name: Ratio of new-grad professional sponsorship-mention rate to the all-full-time Handshake rate
previous_assumptions.rationale: Handshake's 2.6% is measured on full-time postings on an early-career platform, close to but not identical to the target scope. The Trylitos internship subset shows a higher offer rate (0.4%) than the all-posting rate in the same sample (0.1%), and JobShifu's professional functions (software 0.81%, education 1.11%) are several-fold above the all-posting 0.18%, suggesting new-grad professional postings state sponsorship more often; but the target excludes non-professional postings Handshake may include. Net effect uncertain, centred at 1 with a wide range.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to move the Handshake all-full-time rate onto the new-grad professional scope.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: A direct new-grad-specific sponsorship-mention rate materially outside 0.4x-2.5x of 2.6%.

previous_assumptions.name: Sponsorship-mentioning postings per initial-employment H-1B approval
previous_assumptions.rationale: Each initial H-1B approval corresponds to at least one posting that stated sponsorship, but postings are reposted, duplicated across boards, and many sponsorship-mentioning postings never convert to an approval (lottery losses, candidates who do not need sponsorship, roles filled by OPT workers). A ratio of a few postings per approval is the natural order of magnitude; the range spans the plausible deduplication and conversion spread.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert FY2025 initial H-1B approvals into a 2026 posting count, assuming the FY2025 approval level is a reasonable stand-in for 2026 sponsorship activity.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that sponsorship-mentioning postings per approval are below 1 or above 10.

previous_assumptions.name: Adjustment from all-posting JobShifu scope to new-grad professional scope
previous_assumptions.rationale: JobShifu measures sponsorship mentions across all US postings, including hourly and blue-collar roles that almost never sponsor. New-grad professional roles (software, data, engineering, finance, consulting) are far more likely to state sponsorship than the all-posting average, so the all-posting rate must be scaled up. The Trylitos internship subset (0.4% vs 0.1% all-posting) and the JobShifu function table (software 0.81%, education 1.11% vs 0.18% overall) both point to a multiplier of several-fold.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to move the JobShifu all-posting offer share onto the new-grad professional scope.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: A direct new-grad professional sponsorship-mention rate close to the all-posting rate (multiplier near 1).

previous_assumptions.name: Share of 2026 new-grad professional postings that are internships rather than full-time entry-level
previous_assumptions.rationale: The target sums internships and full-time entry-level roles. Internship postings are a substantial but minority share of new-grad professional postings; NACE reports intern hiring growing ~4% and intern-to-full-time conversion at 63%, so internships are a meaningful channel but smaller than full-time entry-level hiring. A quarter of the base is a reasonable central value.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to weight the internship-specific sponsorship rate against the full-time rate in the sum route.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that internships are below 10% or above 45% of new-grad professional postings.

previous_assumptions.name: Ratio of total unique US new-grad professional postings in 2026 to the JobShifu all-posting snapshot size
previous_assumptions.rationale: The JobShifu snapshot reads 1,482,236 US postings at a point in time (Oct 2026). The annual flow of unique new-grad professional postings (internships plus 0-1 year professional roles) is plausibly of the same order as, or smaller than, that all-posting stock: new-grad professional roles are a minority of all postings (14% of unique postings in the three-NY-county sample require 0-1 years; 21-24% of tech postings are entry-level), but the annual flow accumulates over twelve months while the snapshot is a stock. A ratio near 0.5 with a wide range spans the plausible deduplication and scope spread.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert the JobShifu all-posting snapshot into the new-grad professional posting base.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: A direct count of unique US new-grad professional postings for 2026 far outside 0.15x-1.5x of 1.48M.

previous_assumptions.name: Ratio of total unique US new-grad professional postings in 2026 to the Trylitos all-posting sample size
previous_assumptions.rationale: The Trylitos September 2026 sample reads 11,304 US postings from 2,000 employers. The annual flow of unique new-grad professional postings is plausibly of the same order as, or smaller than, that all-posting sample scaled to the national posting universe; new-grad professional roles are a minority of all postings (14% of unique postings in the three-NY-county sample require 0-1 years; 21-24% of tech postings are entry-level), but the annual flow accumulates over twelve months. A ratio near 0.5 with a wide range spans the plausible deduplication and scope spread.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert the Trylitos all-posting sample into the new-grad professional posting base.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: A direct count of unique US new-grad professional postings for 2026 far outside 0.15x-1.5x of 11,304.

final.text:

residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
